headline: New law exempts many federally funded computer chip factory projects from certain federal environmental and historic preservation reviews.
what_it_does: The law says certain computer chip (semiconductor) projects that get federal money under a 2021 defense law do not have to go through reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act or the National Historic Preservation Act. This covers projects that started work by December 31, 2024, projects funded only by federal loans or loan guarantees, and projects where other federal aid is 10% or less of the total cost. It also creates categories of chip factory building, expansion, and upgrade work that are excluded from environmental review. For funded projects that still need review, the Commerce Department can lead the review and may reuse earlier studies and decisions in some cases.

who_it_affects.group: Companies building or expanding chip factories with federal funding
who_it_affects.how: Many of their projects can skip or face shorter federal environmental and historic preservation reviews.

who_it_affects.group: People living near planned chip factories
who_it_affects.how: Some projects near them will no longer go through the federal environmental and historic review process, which can include public input.
It can serve as the lead agency for reviews of funded chip projects that are not exempt and may rely on prior studies.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 2, 2024; one exemption applies to projects whose activities begin by December 31, 2024.
